We are forecasting 2 weeks ahead (from August 14 to August 28). If the series acts as a random walk, the standard deviation over two weeks is approximately 0.58 * sqrt(2) ≈ 0.82. However, there has been a steady downward trend over the past 9 weeks, declining by a total of 3.4 points (an average of -0.38 points per week). A naive linear extrapolation over the next two weeks would predict a further drop of ~0.76 points, leading to a forecast of roughly -25.0. 

2. Inside view. Political trackers rarely move linearly without bound, meaning there will eventually be a floor and some mean reversion. Factoring in a slight continued drag but hedging against a stabilizing floor or potential bounce (much like the +0.9 jump on July 17), I will shade my estimate slightly upward from the naive extrapolation to -24.5.

3. Pre-mortem. If this forecast misses badly, it will likely be because the underlying event causing the steep August drop resolved or reversed, triggering a rapid "snap-back" in the tracker (similar to what occurred on July 17 but larger). Alternatively, an escalating crisis could crash his approval past -26.0. By centering the forecast around -24.5 and expanding the standard deviation slightly to cover typical two-week volatility and the possibility of a rebound, I can account for both scenarios.
